title: Shard-aware spillback router and compact KV-windowing for dashboard reads
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Console dashboard query tails are dominated by complex multi-page requests that touch high-cardinality tenant indexes. For several tenants we see p95/p99 spikes during ad-hoc, large window queries which degrade interactive dashboard performance and increase cost. Existing approach (single generic cache + hedged reads) reduces some tails but still suffers from read amplification and long KV cache churn for variable window sizes.

Goal: Build a shard-aware spillback routing layer plus a compact KV-windowing cache in the dashboard query API to reduce tail latency and cache eviction churn while keeping overall read amplification under control. This ticket covers the backend router, a compact in-memory window compaction scheme, and a controlled canary rollout. The focus is production-safe incremental rollout, observability, and measurable SLO improvements (p95/p99).

High-level idea: When a request exceeds a configured cardinality/scan threshold or requests large page windows, the query router spills the request back to a small set of dedicated "compact" query workers that use a compact KV-window representation: variable-size prefix buckets + coalesced snapshot pointers. Those workers perform windowed materialization with aggressive coalescing across nearby sequence ranges, maintain tenant-aware TTLs, and expose a fast read path for paginated cursors. The router is shard-aware: it routes based on tenant cardinality and index density so hot tenants are routed to dedicated compact workers, avoiding noisy-neighbor eviction in the general cache pool.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for large-window dashboard queries reduced by >= 30% in canary tenants compared to baseline
overall cache miss rate for dashboard index lookups decreases or stays within +/- 5% of baseline after canary
no regression in small-window interactive queries (p50/p95 within 5% of baseline)
rolled out behind a feature flag with canary gating and automatic rollback on SLO breach
integration tests cover cursor consistency across spillback and normal paths
implementation_notes:
Router changes: add a spillback decision stage in the existing query router that evaluates: estimated scanned rows, tenant cardinaility score, current cache eviction pressure, and recent tail-latency signals. Decision is a simple score with tunable thresholds (config via runtime flags).

Compact workers: implement a compact KV-window store that keeps compressed prefix buckets (variable bucket sizes depending on sequence density) and snapshot pointers to underlying materialized segments. Provide APIs: GetWindow(cursor, start, limit), RefreshPrefix(prefixKey), EvictTenant(tenantId). The store will favor coalesced reads and return partial windows if necessary to preserve SLOs.

Consistency: use read-through snapshotting at query time; if a compact worker reads stale data beyond acceptable staleness window the router can fallback to full read path. We'll instrument an 'staleness score' and expose it in telemetry.

Trade-offs: memory vs latency (compact buckets add CPU to recombine); complexity vs stability (introduces another worker pool). We'll mitigate with small initial pool size, conservative thresholds, and slow ramping of canary percentage.
tasks: Design RFC for spillback routing + compact KV-window (doc link in links)
Implement router decision stage and feature flag gating
Implement compact worker in dashboard-query service with compact bucket store
Add tenant cardinality scoring pipeline (fast estimate from usage telemetry)
Write unit and integration tests for cursor continuity across paths
Create dashboards and alerts for p50/p95/p99, cache hit rate, evictions, and spillback ratio
Canary rollout to 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated SLO checks and rollback hooks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal QA on staging with synthetic large-window traces. Phase 1: enable feature flag for internal Canary tenants (5%) and monitor 48 hours. Gate: no SLO breaches and cache miss within +/-5%. Phase 2: expand to 25% with stricter alerting on evictions and memory usage. Phase 3: full rollout with adaptive threshold tuning. Automated rollback: if p99 increases by >15% for any two consecutive 10-minute windows, flip flag off and migrate in-flight cursors back to primary path.
